feedback: Written before this candidate races. The evidence is iteration 0 and iteration 1. Iteration 1 showed that widening the row to x = -0.024 to +0.024 m raised oval progress from 0.18 to 0.95 and s-bend progress from 0.14 to 0.38, so keep that row. Its remaining limits are these. On the s-bend, max_error reached 0.064 m, which is above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and steering_oscillation was 0.265. On the slalom, line_loss_events was exactly 2.0 in all 20 trials, and progress stayed at 0.12. This points to the 12 mm footprint seeing too little tape on sharp alternations. Note that the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). For body_width up to 0.18 m, that gives at most 0.0575 m, so the limit stays at 0.06 m and body width is not a useful lever. The sensor size change to 0.016 m is the one I am carrying into this candidate. Wheel_track matters because turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a shorter track gives more yaw response per unit of wheel differential. Yaw inertia depends only on mass and body dimensions. Depending on the next race: if slalom line_loss_events fall below 2.0 with the larger footprint, keep sensor_size 0.016. If they stay at 2.0 and max_error still reaches 0.06 m, yaw response is the limit, so test wheel_track 0.10 m. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 on the s-bend with no change in losses, try reducing mass to 0.6 kg rather than changing the sensors.
requested_changes: Keep the widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m at y = 0.04 m), which raised progress on all three tracks in iteration 1, and keep sensor_size 0.016 m.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at 2.0 and max_error stays at or above 0.06 m after the sensor change, try wheel_track 0.10 m, because iteration 1 shows the s-bend and slalom are limited by yaw response.

If steering_oscillation on the s-bend rises above about 0.3 without fewer line losses, try mass 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia. Do not change body_width, since it does not move the off-track limit within its allowed range.
